topic.title: Generative AI Basics
topic.description: Understand how LLMs work, what they can do, and where they fall short.

items.prompt: What does 'Generative AI' fundamentally do?
options: Searches the internet and returns existing web pages
Stores and retrieves data from a fixed database
Produces new content (text, images, code, audio, video) based on patterns learned from training data

items.prompt: Which of these is NOT a generative AI capability?
options: Writing essays from a topic prompt
Guaranteeing 100% factually accurate answers to every question

items.prompt: What is the KEY difference between generative AI and traditional ('discriminative') AI?
options: Generative AI runs on GPUs; discriminative AI runs on CPUs
Generative AI creates new outputs; discriminative AI classifies or predicts from inputs
Generative AI is free; discriminative AI is paid

items.prompt: Which is a TRUE statement about modern generative AI models?
options: They learn statistical patterns from data but do not 'understand' meaning the way humans do
They have true consciousness and emotions
They access the live internet by default
They store every training example verbatim

items.prompt: Why did Generative AI explode into mainstream around 2022-2023?
options: The transformer architecture + huge models + massive compute + chat interfaces finally produced human-quality outputs at scale
The internet finally got fast enough
AI was invented in 2022 for the first time

items.prompt: What does 'LLM' stand for?
At the core, what does an LLM actually DO when generating text?
options: Asks another LLM and copies the response
Predicts the next token (word fragment) based on all previous tokens, one token at a time
Translates the question into machine code and runs it
Looks up the answer in a database

items.prompt: What is a 'parameter' in an LLM?
options: A learnable numerical weight that the model adjusts during training; modern LLMs have billions
A setting the user adjusts in the UI

items.prompt: What does a model's 'training cutoff date' mean?
options: The model gets retrained every day
The model has no knowledge of events that happened after that date
The model stops working on that date
Users can't access the model past that date

items.prompt: Which is a famous LLM family?
What is a 'token' in the context of LLMs?
options: A unit of text the model processes — often a word, sub-word, or punctuation mark

items.prompt: Roughly how many tokens does one average English word use?
Why do LLMs charge by tokens instead of by words?
options: Tokens are the actual unit of computation the model processes, so cost scales linearly with tokens
Words don't exist in all languages
Words are too hard to count

items.prompt: Which type of text typically uses the MOST tokens per character?
options: Non-English text and code with many special characters or rare words

items.prompt: What is a 'tokenizer'?
options: The component that splits raw text into tokens (and back) before/after the model processes it

items.prompt: What is 'pretraining' for an LLM?
options: Training the model on a massive corpus of text to learn general language patterns
Training the user before they use the model
Pre-installing the model on hardware before shipping

items.prompt: What is 'fine-tuning' an LLM?
options: Further training a pretrained model on a smaller, specialized dataset to specialize its behavior
Adjusting the volume of the model's voice

items.prompt: What does 'RLHF' stand for?
Why doesn't training data include the live internet?
options: Training is illegal on live data
Training happens once on a fixed snapshot; live updates would be impractical and unsafe
The internet is too expensive to download

items.prompt: What is the role of GPUs in training LLMs?
options: They display the training progress on screen
They perform the massive parallel matrix math required, far faster than CPUs

items.prompt: What architectural breakthrough enabled modern LLMs?
options: The Transformer (introduced in 'Attention Is All You Need', 2017)

items.prompt: What does 'attention' do in a transformer?
options: Lets each token weigh its relationship to every other token in the context to capture meaning
Listens to the user with a microphone
Watches the screen for the user

items.prompt: Why are transformers parallelizable in training?
options: They use multiple programming languages at once
Self-attention processes all tokens simultaneously, unlike sequential RNNs

items.prompt: What are the THREE main components of attention math?
Which of these is also based on the transformer architecture?
options: BERT, T5, GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama — virtually all modern major language models

items.prompt: Which is a STRONG suit of modern LLMs?
options: Replacing all human experts in medicine
Summarizing long documents into concise key points

items.prompt: What can image generation models (DALL-E, Midjourney, Imagen) do?
options: Create novel images from text descriptions, in many styles and compositions

items.prompt: Which of these has Generative AI become especially good at since 2024?
options: Writing functional code from natural-language descriptions

items.prompt: What's a realistic use of generative AI for productivity?
options: Drafting emails, summarizing meetings, generating first drafts of reports

items.prompt: Which is a NEW capability in 2024-2025 generative AI?
options: Long-context reasoning, native multimodality (text+image+audio+video), and agentic tool use

items.prompt: What is a 'hallucination' in generative AI?
options: The model generates plausible-sounding information that is actually false or invented
The model shows ASCII art accidentally
The model translates to a wrong language

items.prompt: Which task do LLMs struggle with WITHOUT tools?
Why might an LLM give DIFFERENT answers to the same question?
options: Sampling randomness (temperature) introduces variability in token selection

items.prompt: What ethical concern is associated with LLMs being trained on internet data?
options: They become too polite to be useful
They can absorb and replicate human biases, stereotypes, and copyrighted content

items.prompt: What is a key reason NOT to use LLMs for high-stakes decisions alone?
options: They are probabilistic and lack accountability — a human should remain responsible for critical outcomes

items.prompt: What is the FIRST thing every interaction with an LLM requires?
options: A prompt — the input text that asks or instructs the model

items.prompt: Which prompt produces the BEST output?
options: 'Write a 3-paragraph beginner-friendly guide to budgeting for university students in Pakistan.'

items.prompt: What role does 'context' play in a prompt?
options: Providing relevant background helps the model produce on-target, accurate responses
Context is illegal in some prompts

items.prompt: What does 'show your work' or 'think step by step' do in a prompt?
options: Makes the model use a different font
Triggers Chain-of-Thought reasoning, often improving accuracy on multi-step problems
Forces the model to respond in code

items.prompt: What is the BEST way to learn good prompting?
options: Practice, iterate, and observe — try variations and see what changes the output

items.prompt: Which is a popular general-purpose chat-based AI?
Which tool category does Midjourney belong to?
What is GitHub Copilot?
options: A backup tool for GitHub repos
An AI pair-programming assistant that suggests code as you type in your editor

items.prompt: Which tool is designed for AI-powered web search?
What is 'open source' in the context of LLMs?
options: Models whose weights are publicly downloadable and can be self-hosted (e.g., Llama, Mistral, Qwen)

items.prompt: What is 'multimodal' AI?
options: An AI that can accept and/or produce multiple input/output types (text, image, audio, video) in one model
An AI that runs on multiple devices simultaneously
An AI translated to multiple languages
An AI with multiple installation modes

items.prompt: What can you do with a vision-capable LLM?
options: Upload an image and ask questions about it: describe it, extract text, identify objects, analyze charts
Convert the image to a video

items.prompt: What's a realistic use case for multimodal AI?
options: Extracting structured data from receipts, invoices, or screenshots

items.prompt: What is 'text-to-speech' (TTS) generative AI?
options: AI that converts written text into natural-sounding spoken audio
AI that talks back to humans

items.prompt: What is 'text-to-video' generative AI?
options: AI that creates short video clips from text descriptions (Sora, Veo, Runway)

items.prompt: What is an 'AI agent'?
options: A human salesperson for AI products
An AI system that can autonomously plan, use tools, and take multi-step actions to accomplish a goal

items.prompt: Which is an example of an AI agent task?
options: 'Book a flight to Karachi under $400 for next Friday, then email me the confirmation.'

items.prompt: What is 'function calling' / 'tool use' in LLMs?
options: The model writes its own Python and runs it directly
The model bills the user for each call
The model returns a structured request for the host application to run an external function (API call, database query, etc.)

items.prompt: What is the risk of fully autonomous AI agents?
options: They can take incorrect, irreversible actions without human review

items.prompt: Which is a popular framework for building AI agents?
options: LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI Assistants API

items.prompt: What is 'RAG' in generative AI?
options: Retrieval-Augmented Generation — fetching relevant documents and injecting them into the prompt before the model answers

items.prompt: Why use RAG instead of fine-tuning for a company knowledge base?
options: RAG lets you update knowledge instantly without retraining and grounds answers in verifiable sources

items.prompt: What is a 'vector database' in RAG systems?
options: A database for graphic vectors only
A specialized database storing text as numerical embeddings, enabling semantic similarity search

items.prompt: What are 'embeddings'?
options: Numerical representations of text (vectors) that capture semantic meaning for similarity comparison

items.prompt: When does RAG go WRONG?
options: When the model speaks too quietly
When retrieval returns irrelevant or misleading documents, causing the model to confidently generate wrong answers from bad sources
When the model is too polite

items.prompt: What is 'AI bias'?
options: When AI users are biased against AI
When AI runs faster on certain CPUs
When AI systems reflect or amplify unfair patterns present in their training data

items.prompt: What is 'AI alignment'?
options: The research field focused on making AI systems behave in line with human values and intentions
Aligning AI fonts on a webpage
Aligning AI hardware in a server rack
Setting AI to the correct time zone

items.prompt: Which is a RESPONSIBLE practice for AI product builders?
options: Implement safety filters, rate limits, transparency about AI use, and clear user feedback mechanisms

items.prompt: Why is 'deepfake' technology a serious concern?
options: It is too slow to be a problem
It can create convincing fake images, audio, and video of real people, enabling fraud and misinformation
It only works for fictional characters

items.prompt: What's an important question to ask before deploying AI in a sensitive domain?
options: 'What color should the AI's logo be?'
'How many emojis should the AI use?'
'What happens if the AI is wrong, and who is accountable?'

items.prompt: Why should you be cautious about sharing sensitive data with public AI chatbots?
options: Chatbots are legally bound to secrecy
Inputs may be logged, used for training, or accessed by the provider — treat them like public posts

items.prompt: What is 'data residency' in AI?
options: Where AI models physically live in homes
The country/region where AI providers store and process user data, which has legal implications (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.)

items.prompt: Which is a PRIVACY-FRIENDLY option for using LLMs at work?
options: Self-hosted open-source models, or enterprise plans with explicit no-training clauses
Sharing API keys with everyone in the company
Free public chatbots with all company data pasted in
Posting sensitive prompts on social media

items.prompt: What is the safest way to share PII (personally identifiable information) with an LLM?
options: PII is fine to share publicly
Always include all PII for context
Redact or pseudonymize the PII first; only share what's strictly needed

items.prompt: What does 'opt-out of training' mean in AI APIs?
options: A setting (or contractual term) that prevents the provider from using your data to train future models

items.prompt: Which is a HIGH-LEVERAGE personal use of generative AI?
options: Replacing all human relationships with AI
Letting AI make all your decisions automatically
Drafting first versions of emails, documents, and content you then edit

items.prompt: What is 'meeting summarization' AI?
options: AI that joins meetings as a participant
AI that transcribes a meeting and produces a concise summary with action items and decisions

items.prompt: Which is a SMART way to use AI for learning?
options: Ask AI to explain concepts in multiple ways, generate practice problems, and quiz yourself
Have AI take exams for you
Believe everything AI says without checking

items.prompt: What's a PITFALL of relying too heavily on AI for writing?
options: Skill atrophy — if you stop thinking, your own writing and analysis abilities weaken over time

items.prompt: Which is a GOOD workflow for AI-assisted coding?
options: Have AI draft code, then review, test, and verify it carefully — never ship code you don't understand
Never let AI write any code
Ship AI code straight to production untested

items.prompt: How do LLM APIs typically charge?
options: Per million tokens of input and output, with different prices for each

items.prompt: Which is a way to get high-quality generative AI for FREE?
options: Asking your friend to share their password
Free tiers of Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, Groq, Copilot, plus open-source models you can self-host

items.prompt: Why is generating a long response MORE expensive than a short one?
options: Servers charge more for long files
Long responses use a different model
Each generated token requires a separate forward pass through the model

items.prompt: Which factor will MOST reduce your AI API bill?
options: Using more expensive models for simple tasks
Sending each word as a separate API call

items.prompt: What is 'inference' in AI?
options: Running a trained model to generate a response — distinct from training

items.prompt: Which is the BEST mental model for using AI?
options: A brilliant but inexperienced intern — fast, eager, but needs supervision and clear instructions
A magic black box you should never question
A search engine with verified answers
A perfect oracle that's always right

items.prompt: What is 'human-in-the-loop' (HITL) AI?
options: AI systems where humans review, approve, or correct AI outputs at critical points
AI that needs human power to run

items.prompt: Which jobs are LEAST likely to be fully replaced by current AI?
options: All jobs are equally at risk
Roles requiring physical presence, emotional judgment, accountability, and novel reasoning under uncertainty

items.prompt: What's a HEALTHY mindset toward AI in your career?
options: Refuse to use any AI ever
Learn to use AI as a multiplier on your existing skills; treat it as a tool, not a threat or a savior
Believe AI will solve every problem automatically

items.prompt: Which is TRUE about AI literacy in 2026?
options: It's becoming a baseline skill — like email and Excel were in previous eras
It's a fad that will pass soon

sub_pools.name: AI in business and creative work

items.prompt: Which business function has AI rapidly transformed?
options: Customer support (chatbots, ticket triage, agent assist)

items.prompt: What is 'AI marketing copywriting'?
options: Using AI to draft ad copy, email subject lines, social posts, and product descriptions at scale

items.prompt: Which is a creative use of generative AI?
options: Brainstorming, generating image references, drafting story outlines, exploring 'what if' variations

items.prompt: What's a key copyright concern with AI-generated content?
options: AI content is always public domain
AI content has no copyright issues anywhere
AI content always belongs to OpenAI
Legal status of AI output and training data is still evolving; commercial use should be reviewed carefully

items.prompt: Why do many companies have an 'AI usage policy'?
options: To clarify what data can be shared with AI, what AI output can be used commercially, and how to disclose AI assistance
To restrict AI to executives only

items.prompt: What does 'AGI' stand for?
options: Artificial General Intelligence — AI matching or exceeding human cognitive ability across most domains

items.prompt: What is 'multimodal native' AI?
options: AI made in the user's home country
Models built from the ground up to handle text, images, audio, and video as first-class inputs and outputs
AI that only works in native languages

items.prompt: Which trend is making AI more affordable?
options: Smaller, more efficient models that match larger models on common tasks at a fraction of the cost

items.prompt: What is 'on-device AI'?
options: AI that requires a specific device store
AI models running directly on your phone or laptop, with no cloud round-trip

items.prompt: Which is a REALISTIC near-term AI development?
options: AI that eliminates need for any human work
AI agents that complete multi-step tasks across multiple apps autonomously
AI that solves all of physics

items.prompt: What's the FIRST step for someone new to generative AI?
options: Pick a free chatbot (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) and use it daily for real tasks to build intuition

items.prompt: Which is a GREAT first project to learn AI?
options: Launch a $1M startup before writing any code
Build a small tool that automates a real annoying task in your own life or work
Try to recreate GPT-4 from scratch
Memorize the math behind transformers first

items.prompt: Where can you learn AI for FREE?
options: Only by working at AI labs
DeepLearning.AI, freeCodeCamp, Hugging Face, Anthropic Docs, OpenAI Cookbook, YouTube channels

items.prompt: Which community is GOOD for AI learners?
options: Hugging Face forums, Reddit r/LocalLLaMA, AI Discord servers, Twitter/X AI builders

items.prompt: What's the MOST important meta-skill for working with AI long-term?
options: Memorizing one specific model version forever
Avoiding all new tools after the first one you learn
Curiosity and the willingness to keep learning as the field evolves rapidly
